header.name: gather
header.tagline: Research intake for gated APIs, paywalls, JS pages, and scanned PDFs.

flows.title: How a closed manifest becomes evidence somebody else can check
flows.alt: Eight stages from a validated manifest to a network-free re-check. A source whose extracted values are not found on the fetched page is dropped before anything is stored. The re-check reports match, corrupt or missing.
flows.footnote: A source that fails the grounding check is dropped and the run says so. The last stage needs no network.

stages.title: Manifest
stages.note: A closed list of sources, validated before anything is fetched.

stages.title: Capture
stages.note: Each source is fetched on its own, so one failure cannot spread.

stages.title: Extract
stages.note: Schema fields are read from the page that was actually fetched.

stages.title: Ground
stages.note: Every value must appear on that page, matched on word boundaries.

stages.title: Store
stages.note: Bodies are filed under the sha256 of their own content.

stages.title: Receipt
stages.note: One appended row per distinct receipt, sealed over the set.

stages.title: Report
stages.note: A canonical, redacted view, meant to be handed to someone.

stages.title: Re-check
stages.note: Re-verified from the artifacts alone, no network in the loop.

returns.label: REQUIRED FIELD MISSING OR NOT ON THE PAGE: SOURCE DROPPED

outcomes.label: MATCH
outcomes.note: the stored body still hashes to its receipt

outcomes.label: CORRUPT
outcomes.note: the body no longer hashes to its receipt

outcomes.label: MISSING
outcomes.note: the receipt points at a body that is not there

cards.kicker: install a backend, or be told you did not
cards.title: What serves each capability, and what happens when nothing does
cards.alt: A card of the four capabilities gather can be asked for. fetch is always served by the stdlib. fast-parse falls back to the stdlib parser, which returns the same answer more slowly. js-render and stealth are refused with a reason when no backend is installed, and the js-render row is marked because it is the one where a plausible fake exists.
heads: what that means for the answer

fields.note: Always served. The core registers this itself, so there is no absent case to report.
Parsing still happens and the answer is the same. What the missing backend costs is time, not truth.
Marked because this is the row where a plausible fake exists: the static shell. It is never returned dressed as a render.
Refused the same way. A request that needed browser impersonation is reported unmet, not answered plainly.

cards.footnote: The refusal is a result object, not an exception: status UNVERIFIABLE, the capability asked for, and a reason reading no backend for capability js-render. It carries no html and no content hash, so nothing downstream mistakes it for a page that was fetched. Which backends are installed differs by machine, so this draws the absent case, which is the same everywhere. Refusing honestly says nothing about how well an installed backend renders.
